My contribution

Animation, speech
and text that stays usable.

I integrated Three.js rendering, responsive camera behaviour, authored animation states, speech playback and audio/transcript-driven facial targets. I blended gestures so the character does not jump straight between unrelated poses.

The assistant uses a maintained professional source of truth. Browser recognition and recorded-audio transcription offer different input paths, while the readable chat survives optional model or WebGL failure. The 3D model loads only when the viewer is requested.

What you can inspect.

Implementation

  • Three.js rendering, GLB animation and morph targets.
  • Blended authored gestures and approximate mouth cues.
  • Typed questions, browser speech and recording fallback.
  • Server-side chat and transcription functions.

Authorship and assets

Engineering, state orchestration and integration are documented separately from adapted animation resources and AI-assisted visual references. The source-code MIT licence does not grant reuse of the character likeness, model or identity artwork.

Read the asset provenance ↗

What this does—and doesn’t—show.

The character is not a person and AI replies are not Sadeq speaking personally. Answers can be incorrect. Controlled context narrows the subject; it cannot guarantee truth. Mouth movement is approximate, not phoneme-perfect lip sync.

Microphone and speech features vary by browser and permission state. In the actual app, recordings are used to transcribe the current question; provider processing is remote. These teaching views make no microphone, recording, model-loading or provider request.

The map is a reviewed overview of source revision cc7771f, not a continuously updated dependency graph.
